tool_analysis:
1) Step Analysis: The recorded steps perform a complete end-to-end Magento 1.9 admin product creation flow. They start from about:blank, navigate to the catalog products admin URL, encounter the login page, enter admin credentials, and submit the login form. After authentication, the flow lands on Catalog > Manage Products grid, locates and clicks the Add Product button, reaches the New Product initialization page, confirms Attribute Set and Product Type selectors, and clicks Continue to open the full New Product form. On the main product form, the agent fills the required fields on the General tab (name, description, short description, SKU, weight, status, visibility), then switches to the Prices tab to set price and tax class, then to the Inventory tab to set quantity and stock availability, and finally clicks Save. The save redirects back to the Manage Products grid, where a success message and the new product row confirm product creation.

2) Task Definition: The tool’s purpose is to deterministically create a new simple product in Magento 1.9 admin, starting from the catalog_product grid URL, using stable selectors and robust navigation. It must handle login if the session is unauthenticated, initiate the add-product flow, select an attribute set and product type, fill the key General, Prices, and Inventory fields with parameterized values, and save the product, returning to the Manage Products grid where the product is persisted.

3) Action Plan:
- Navigate directly to the catalog_product grid URL.
- Handle login page: input username and password into the correct fields and click the login button using robust selectors (NOT the previously failing input[name="login[username]"][type="text"] selector). Use element indices / hashes captured: username element_hash=3597a5c5e6, password element_hash=1c47a5217e, login submit element_hash=6831836d17, and also add label-based CSS selectors as backup.
- Once on Manage Products grid, click the Add Product button in the header using a robust selector scoped to div.content-header (not by generic index like 0). Use element_hash=066c08a170 as deterministic anchor and CSS selector div.content-header a.scalable.add or button[title='Add Product'].
- On the New Product initialization page (/admin/catalog_product/new/), optionally select the desired Attribute Set and Product Type via dropdowns (parameterized), using standard Magento selectors select#attribute_set_id / select[name='set'] and select#product_type / select[name='type'], then click the Continue button (element_hash=b34f76fda3, button[title='Continue']).
- On the resulting New Product form (/admin/catalog_product/new/set/{set_id}/type/{type}/), fill:
  - General tab fields (Name, Description, Short Description, SKU, Weight, Status, Visibility) using their captured element_hashes and standard name-based selectors (product[name], product[description], product[short_description], product[sku], product[weight], product[status], product[visibility]).
  - Switch to Prices tab and set Price and Tax Class using element_hashes and selectors (input for product[price], select for product[tax_class_id]).
  - Switch to Inventory tab and set Qty and Stock Availability using element_hashes and selectors (product[stock_data][qty], product[stock_data][is_in_stock]).
- Click Save using the Save button in the header (element_hash=a97b21d113, button[title='Save']).
- Optionally confirm success by ensuring we’re back on Manage Products grid.

4) Variable Identification:
Essential inputs for this tool based on the flow:
- login_username: Magento admin username (text). Required because session may be unauthenticated; in the demo it was 'admin'.
- login_password: Magento admin password (text). Required; in the demo it was 'password123'.
- attribute_set: visible text of the attribute set to use on the initialization page (e.g., 'Default', 'Electronics'). Optional with default 'Default'.
- product_type: visible text of product type (e.g., 'Simple Product', 'Configurable Product'). Optional with default 'Simple Product', but this tool is primarily intended for simple products.
- product_name: Name field value.
- product_description: Description field value.
- product_short_description: Short Description field value.
- product_sku: SKU value (must be unique).
- product_weight: numeric weight value as string.
- product_status: visible text value for Status dropdown ('Enabled' or 'Disabled').
- product_visibility: visible text for Visibility dropdown ('Not Visible Individually', 'Catalog', 'Search', 'Catalog, Search').
- product_price: Price field value as string.
- product_tax_class: visible text for Tax Class dropdown (e.g., 'Taxable Goods', 'None').
- product_qty: quantity value as string.
- product_stock_status: visible text for Stock Availability dropdown ('In Stock', 'Out of Stock').

These map directly to specific Magento form fields, minimizing abstraction and matching HTML name/id attributes when known.

5) Step Optimization:
- Navigation: Go directly to http://dockerized-magento.local/index.php/admin/catalog_product/index/ as the starting point; Magento redirects /catalog_product/ to /catalog_product/index/ after save anyway. This avoids unnecessary menu navigation clicks (like going via Sales > Catalog) seen in the run. No extra filtering/sorting/pagination actions are needed for core product creation, so omit them.
- Login: Replace the brittle selector input[name="login[username]"][type="text"] that previously failed with (a) deterministic element hashes from the run and (b) label/attribute-based CSS selectors. Because our tool schema doesn’t expose elementHash for inputs directly, we’ll rely on the recorded element hashes for determinism within steps and include semantic cssSelector/xpath hints; the controller can use either. We also include a short wait after navigation to let the login form render.
- Add Product: Instead of using index 118 (which may shift), use elementHash 066c08a170 and a scoped CSS selector div.content-header a.scalable.add or button[title='Add Product'] so we click the correct control even if indices change.
- For the init step and product form, prefer deterministic interactions via elementHash plus explicit field names. Tabs (General, Prices, Inventory) are addressed via their tab anchors with element hashes: Prices tab element_hash=86ed7ee82d, Inventory tab element_hash=71d44f34a7.
- We do not include exploratory steps like viewing RSS, changing store view, using mass actions, or grid filters, as they are not essential to the core task.
- We also omit the final verification filter/search in the grid; presence of the success message and grid load is sufficient for completion.

The resulting tool is a single-purpose, parameter-driven sequence that logs in if needed, opens Add Product, initializes a simple product using a chosen attribute set and product type, fills necessary data, and saves, using stable selectors that address prior failures.
name: tool_create_product.v3
description: Create a new simple product in Magento 1.9 admin starting from the catalog product grid URL: logs in if needed, opens Add Product, selects attribute set and product type, fills required fields across General, Prices, and Inventory tabs, and saves the product.

steps.description: Navigate directly to the Magento Catalog > Manage Products grid URL to start the add-product flow.
Wait for the page (either login form or Manage Products grid) to load fully.
Handle conditional presence of login form, since the tool may be run with or without an existing admin session. Use robust selectors based on labels 'User Name:' and 'Password:' and the Login button.
steps.task: If the admin login form is visible, enter username and password and submit the form. Otherwise, do nothing and keep the current authenticated session on the Manage Products grid.

steps.description: Wait for post-login navigation to complete and the Manage Products grid to load.
Click the 'Add Product' button in the Manage Products header to initiate the new product workflow.
Wait for the New Product initialization (Create Product Settings) page to load.
Select the desired Attribute Set on the Create Product Settings page using the provided visible text (defaults to 'Default' at runtime if not specified).
Select the desired Product Type (e.g., 'Simple Product') on the Create Product Settings page.
Click the Continue button to proceed from Create Product Settings to the full New Product form.
Wait for the full New Product form to load with the General tab visible.
Fill the Name field on the General tab with the provided product_name.
Fill the Description field on the General tab with the provided product_description.
Fill the Short Description field on the General tab with the provided product_short_description.
Fill the SKU field on the General tab with the provided product_sku.
Fill the Weight field on the General tab with the provided numeric product_weight.
Select the Status value (e.g., 'Enabled' or 'Disabled') on the General tab.
Select the Visibility value (e.g., 'Catalog, Search') on the General tab.
Switch to the Prices tab of the New Product form.
Wait for the Prices tab fields to become visible.
Fill the Price field on the Prices tab with the provided product_price.
Select the Tax Class on the Prices tab using the provided visible text (e.g., 'Taxable Goods').
Switch to the Inventory tab to set quantity and stock status.
Wait for the Inventory tab fields to become visible.
Fill the Qty field on the Inventory tab with the provided product_qty.
Set the Stock Availability on the Inventory tab (e.g., 'In Stock').
Click the Save button to persist the new product and return to the Manage Products grid.
Wait for the save operation to complete and for the Manage Products grid (with success message) to reload.
Optionally verify the outcome by extracting the success message after saving the product.
steps.goal: Capture confirmation text indicating the product was saved (e.g., 'The product has been saved.') for logging or verification.
